Scroll One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao San Da Fu, Shi...

Translated by the Imperial Preceptor for Transmitting the Dharma, the Great Master, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject Dharmapāla, and others, by imperial decree. Chapter One: The Secret Body of the Bodhisattva (Bodhisattvakāyaguhyapaṭala), Part One. Thus have I heard:

At one time the Blessed One was dwelling on Vulture Peak Mountain in the city of Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of forty-two thousand bhikṣus and eighty-four thousand bodhisattvas—all of whom had already attained supernatural powers and sublime wisdom—great bodhisattvas...
This assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas has all come from various Buddha-fields in other directions;
they have attained forbearance (*kṣānti*), are non-retrogressive (*avaivartika*), and are in their final birth before Buddhahood (*ekajātipratibaddha*).

They have acquired all *dhāraṇīs* and *samādhis*, possess unimpeded eloquence (*pratisaṃvid*), are able to skillfully transcend boundless Buddha-fields, and are proficient in the ten directions throughout the infinite.
They establish and manifest themselves within all Buddha-fields, sporting with sovereign mastery through the wisdom of supernormal powers;

they subdue all Māras and refute all heterodox arguments; they thoroughly understand the mental activities of all sentient beings, and furthermore, through supreme wisdom, skillfully discern the faculties of others, penetrating and entering the principles and teachings of all *pāramitās*.
This Dharma gate is endowed with skillful means, reaching the ultimate, most supreme further shore, and is praised by all Buddhas together;

throughout immeasurable, boundless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of kalpas, one has accumulated the practices of the path to ultimate enlightenment; one’s mind is as impartial as earth, water, fire, wind, and space, which is boundless; having well-cultivated the contemplation of loving-kindness in accordance with reality, one is able to transcend all attachments and obstacles that arise.

They shall obtain the wondrous and excellent physical marks of Nārāyaṇa, possessing a body as firm and indestructible as a vajra; they shall be able to roar the lion’s roar and proclaim the sounds of the Dharma, attaining supreme fearlessness amidst all assemblies of the great multitude, and possessing a great radiance that eclipses the sun and moon.

Having attained the equality of the three times regarding all phenomena as they have been taught, they skillfully expound the most supreme and profound essentials of the Dharma through their definitive wisdom. They have deeply entered the gateway of all dependently originated phenomena and remain far removed from the two extreme views of nihilism and eternalism. Whether entering or arising from meditative concentrations (*dhyāna*), liberations (*vimokṣa*), samādhis, or samāpattis, they are fully cognizant of them. Their merit, wisdom, and renown pervade the ten directions; they uphold the sovereign jewel of the most supreme True Dharma, ensuring that the noble lineage of the Triple Gem remains unbroken.

Such are the immeasurable, superior practices of merit and wisdom they have accumulated—their names being: Bodhisattva Ratnottama, Bodhisattva Candradhvaja, Bodhisattva Śītaladhvaja, Bodhisattva Prabhādhvaja, Bodhisattva Śrīprabha, Bodhisattva Śrīkūṭa, Bodhisattva Śrīgupta, and N...
The Bodhisattva Rāyaṇadeva, the Bodhisattva Nāgasaṃpraharṣa, the Bodhisattva Nāgottama, the Bodhisattva Nāgārjuna,
the Bodhisattva Surūpadhara, the Bodhisattva Divaukasa, the Bodhisattva Guṇaprabharāja, the Bodhisattva Prabhāpāṇi,
the Bodhisattva Nityotkṣiptahasta, the Bodhisattva Nityādhaḥkṛtahasta, and the Bodhisattva Ratnamudrāhasta.
...Sattva, Ratnapāṇi Bodhisattva, Samantaprabha Bodhisattva, Tārārāja Bodhisattva, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva,
Vajramati Bodhisattva, Vajramahāmatis Bodhisattva, Vajrapada Bodhisattva, Acalapadavikrama Bodhisattva, Trailokyapadavikrama Bodhisattva, Anantapada Bodhisattva...
Bodhisattva Anantamati, Bodhisattva Sūkṣmamati, Bodhisattva Dṛḍhamati, Bodhisattva Devamati,
Bodhisattva Jvalanmati, Bodhisattva Varāgrāmati, Bodhisattva Vardhamānamati, Bodhisattva Nityakaruṇa,
Bodhisattva Nityapramudita, Bodhisattva Pramuditendriya, and Bodhisattva Pāpavināśana.
The Bodhisattva Gati, the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, the Bodhisattva Vimalaprabhāsvasamdhāra,
the Bodhisattva Vīryavikrama, the Bodhisattva Prajñākūṭa, the Bodhisattva Nityodyukta,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta, the Bodhisattva Sumerukalpa, and the Bodhisattva Gaganagañja.
Aśocana Bodhisattva, Aniṣpratikāṅkṣin Bodhisattva, Ratnottama Bodhisattva, Ratnacintin Bodhisattva, Sucintin Bodhisattva,
Sucintārtha Bodhisattva, Niyatārtha Bodhisattva, Dhāraṇīśvararāja Bodhisattva, Kṣitigarbha Bodhisattva, Vyūharāja Bodhisattva, and Kṣetra... [Bodhisattva].
The Bodhisattva Earth-Adornment, the Bodhisattva Jewel-Heap, the Bodhisattva Secret-Cave, the Bodhisattva Śakra, the Bodhisattva Varuṇa,
the Bodhisattva Brahma-Net, the Bodhisattva Radiance-Net, the Bodhisattva Celestial-Crown,
the Bodhisattva Wondrous-Arm, the Bodhisattva Wondrous-Eye, the Bodhisattva Fragrant-Elephant, and the Elephant Among [Elephants]...
Gandhahastin Bodhisattva, Siṃhadhvaja Bodhisattva, Arthasiddhimati Bodhisattva, Sāgaramati Bodhisattva,
Susaṃprasthita Bodhisattva, Śāntamati Bodhisattva, Maitreya Bodhisattva, and Mañjuśrīkumārabhūta Bodhisattva.

Thus, this assembly of eighty-four thousand great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as the Brahma kings, Śakra devānām indra, and the world-protecting devas of this trichiliocosm, together with other hosts of celestial kings of great majesty and power—whether they were hosts of nāga kings, yakṣa kings, asura kings, garuḍa kings, kiṃnara kings, mahoraga kings, or gandharva kings—all such hosts gathered there in assembly.

The nāga kings Anavatapta, Sāgara, Varuṇa, Manasvin, Takṣaka, Suvarṇa, Anantavarṇa, and Susīma—these nāga kings, together with their retinues of many hundreds of thousands of nāgas, came to this assembly to attend upon the World-Honored One, pay him homage, and listen to the Dharma.

Furthermore, the assembly of asura kings—namely, Rāhu Asura King, Vemacitra Asura King, Subāhu Asura King, Sāla Asura King, Tāra Asura King, Śīlavat Asura King, Mahāhasa Asura King, Pṛthukukṣi Asura King, and Antakara Asura King—these asura kings, together with their retinues of many hundreds of thousands of asuras, came to this assembly to approach the World-Honored One, pay homage, and listen to the Dharma.

At that time, King Ajātaśatru, the ruler of the kingdom of Magadha, together with his consorts and retinue, came to this assembly to attend upon the World-Honored One, pay homage, and listen to the Dharma.
The fourfold assembly—bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—as well as others, all gathered together.

Furthermore, the various devas dwelling on earth, the devas of the desire and form realms, and the Śuddhāvāsa devas, along with their hosts of sons, also all came to the assembly to attend upon the World-Honored One, pay homage, and listen to the Dharma.

At that time, the World-Honored One was amidst a great assembly, surrounded by and respectfully attended by countless hundreds of thousands of devas and humans who were listening to his teaching of the Dharma.
The Buddha addressed the great assembly:
"I possess a True Dharma called 'The Pure and Sublime Gateway of the Most Supreme and Victorious Practice Universally Encompassing All Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas.'"
This is because it can bring all practices to fulfillment.
That is to say, if a bodhisattva cultivates the practice of generosity, they are able to mature all sentient beings;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of ethical discipline, they attain the fulfillment of all supreme vows.
If Bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of patience, they will attain the perfection of all the primary and secondary marks;
if Bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of diligence, they will be able to fulfill all Buddha-dharmas;
if Bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of meditative concentration, they can bring all their minds under control.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of wisdom, they are able to sever all afflictions;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of preaching the Dharma, they are able to achieve unimpeded eloquence.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of supreme merit, they are able to nurture all sentient beings;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of sublime wisdom, they are able to achieve unimpeded knowledge;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of śamatha, they are able to bring their mental activities to harmony and tranquility.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of sublime contemplation, they are able to remain far removed from all conceptual discrimination;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of loving-kindness, they attain a mind free from all obstructions;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of compassion, they attain a body and mind that are both free from weariness.
If Bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of joy, they are able to sport freely in the garden of the delight of Dharma;
if Bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of equanimity, they are able to sever both favorable and adverse dharmas;
if Bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of listening to the Dharma, they are able to eliminate all obstacles and burdens.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of renunciation, they are able to abandon all grasping and attachment;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of dwelling in araṇya, they ensure that all wholesome dharmas they perform are never lost or destroyed;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of mindfulness, they are able to attain the various doors of dhāraṇī.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of wisdom, they immediately attain supreme wisdom that skillfully discriminates all phenomena;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of abiding, they immediately attain a mind that is invincible by any;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of progression, they are able to understand all meanings and purposes accordingly.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the four foundations of mindfulness, they are able to investigate the body, feelings, mind, and phenomena;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the four right endeavors, they are able to eliminate all unwholesome dharmas and perfect all wholesome dharmas;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the four bases of psychic power, they attain purity and pliancy of body and mind.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the five faculties, they are able to skillfully know the natures of the faculties of both themselves and others;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the five powers, they will not be overcome or subdued by any afflictions;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the seven factors of enlightenment, they will realize all phenomena as they truly are.
If Bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the Eightfold Noble Path, they are able to transcend all deviant paths;
if Bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the Four Noble Truths, they are able to achieve the dharma of immovability;
if Bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the four analytical knowledges, they are able to sever the hearts of doubt in all sentient beings.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of seeking refuge, they will attain the wisdom of mastery;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of spiritual friends, they will be able to accumulate all merits;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of noble intention, they will not be in conflict with any world.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the profound mind, they will attain supreme excellence in all directions;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of correspondence, they will be able to diligently and courageously rescue and deliver others;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of dwelling in monasteries, they will attain the non-forgetting of whatever Dharma they have heard.
If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of the four means of attraction, they are able to gather in all sentient beings;
if bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of gathering the true Dharma, they are able to ensure that the noble lineage of the Three Jewels is never interrupted;
if bodhisattvas skillfully cultivate the practice of dedication, they are able to adorn and purify buddha-fields.
"If bodhisattvas cultivate the practice of skillful means, they will be able to fulfill the knowledge of all modes.

Thus did the World-Honored One proclaim this vast and sublime Dharma, the pure and wondrous gateway that universally encompasses the most supreme and excellent practices of all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

When the Buddha, the World-Honored One, was preaching this Dharma, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, manifested his majestic spiritual power and stood in attendance to the right of the Buddha.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi addressed the Buddha, saying:
"It is marvelous, World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata has excellently expounded this vast and correct Dharma, the supreme and victorious practice and pure, wondrous gateway that universally encompasses all Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas."
“World-Honored One!

As I understand the meaning and intent of what the Buddha has taught, all the supreme practices attained by bodhisattva-mahāsattvas arise from the two practices of merit and wisdom; one should know that they accordingly enter into these two practices of merit and wisdom.”
Why is this? Because by practicing the conduct of merit, bodhisattvas are able to cause all sentient beings to be free from all obstacles;
and if they practice the conduct of wisdom;
They are able to skillfully expound the essential points of the Dharma for all sentient beings, causing them to give rise to joy.
World-Honored One!
For this reason, the two practices of merit and wisdom of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas should be combined.
Why is this? Because by practicing the cultivation of merit, a bodhisattva is able to fulfill the perfection of skillful means (upāya-pāramitā);
and by practicing the cultivation of wisdom, they are able to fulfill the perfection of insight (prajñā-pāramitā).
Therefore, these two practices constitute the two kinds of noble paths of the bodhisattva, which universally encompass all modes of practice.

When a bodhisattva abides in these paths, they are able to subdue those who are difficult to subdue—the hosts of māras of karma. Having already transcended the paths of all evil māras, the bodhisattva does not regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
"It is precisely this non-retrogressive bodhisattva who is able to skillfully elucidate the profound secrets of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, so that they are not concealed.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śāntamati, from within the assembly, approached the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, and said:
"O Great Lord of Secrets!"
You have constantly attended upon all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas, and you are able to joyfully expound all the secret teachings of the Tathāgatas; we pray that you will initiate this discourse.
This is not a realm entered by Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas, much less by other ordinary worldlings.
When he had spoken thus, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, remained silent.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Śāntamati, having understood this matter, approached the Buddha and said:

“I pray that the World-Honored One will command the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, to elucidate for this assembly the secret Dharma of the Tathāgata, so that the multitude of Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas, having heard it, may rejoice, extensively accumulate the factors conducive to enlightenment (*bodhipākṣika-dharma*), accomplish the secret Dharma of the Tathāgata, and practice in accordance with the truth.”
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, saying:
“I now exhort you: you should skillfully proclaim for the great assembly of this gathering the true Dharma of the bodhisattvas’ secrets and the Tathāgata’s secrets.”
“The great assembly in this gathering all desires to hear it.
Then, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, receiving the Buddha’s holy command, stepped forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
In accordance with the Buddha’s injunction, I shall now proclaim the secret Dharma of the Bodhisattvas and the Tathāgatas, which is the true reality.
Yet, if there are any in this assembly who are able to enter into and realize it even slightly, it is entirely due to the majestic power and spiritual authority established by the World-Honored One.
For example, when the night is shrouded in darkness, the light of a lamp reveals and illuminates all forms and images.

This assembly is likewise: among those who have heard and attained even a slight realization of the true Dharma within the secrets of the Bodhisattvas and the secrets of the Tathāgata, you should know that this is entirely established by the majestic spiritual power of the Tathāgata.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śāntamati, saying:
"O son of good family!"

In this present assembly, it would be most excellent if those who have heard this true Dharma of the secrets of the bodhisattvas and the secrets of the Tathāgata were not to be struck with fear or alarm.
Then, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śāntamati addressed the entire assembly gathered there, saying: "Virtuous ones!
As the Buddha has taught, there are four kinds of inconceivables."

What are the four? First, the inconceivability of karma; second, the inconceivability of nāgas; third, the inconceivability of meditative concentration; and fourth, the inconceivability of the Buddha.
Virtuous one, you should know that among these four, only the Buddha-Tathāgata is inconceivable, supreme, and foremost.
All the dharmas of the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* of all Buddhas are established through these four kinds of inconceivability.
Therefore, you virtuous ones!

Having heard of the inconceivable dharmas of the bodhisattvas and the inconceivable dharmas of the Tathāgata, you should not be startled, terrified, or give rise to fear; rather, you should conceive a mind of supreme, vast, and pure joy.

At that time, through the power of empowerment by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, the Bodhisattva Śāntamati was able to know that the entire assembly in this gathering all had faith and joy in the secret teachings of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and were listening to and receiving them.
Immediately, vast celestial flowers were scattered and rained down, accumulating upon his knees as a universal offering.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, addressed the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Śāntamati, saying:
"You should listen attentively; I shall now speak of the secret, true Dharma of the bodhisattvas."

Śāntamati, you should know that in the past, when our present World-Honored One was dwelling in the bodhisattva stage within the Dharma of the Tathāgata Dīpaṃkara, he received from that Buddha the prophecy of his attainment of anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
From that time forth, I have constantly followed the Śākya Bodhisattva; yet, in all his physical actions, he has never acted otherwise [than correctly], nor have I ever seen any sign of crookedness;
in his speech, he has never acted otherwise, nor have I ever heard him utter false words;
in his mind, he has never acted otherwise, nor have I ever known any fault of attachment.
He manifests the signs of dignified deportment through his physical actions solely for the sake of maturing all sentient beings, yet he does not praise himself.

Because the signs of that bodhisattva’s physical deportment are boundless, even all the various modes of conduct of all sentient beings are entirely contained within the signs of the bodhisattva’s deportment; and the bodhisattva, without exerting effort and without needing to arouse further realization, dwells in tranquil composure.
For those sentient beings who are to be liberated through meditative concentration, he manifests meditative concentration to deliver them;
for those who are to be liberated through drums, music, and song, he manifests drums, music, and song to deliver them;
for those who are to be liberated by means of the body of a young boy, he manifests that body to deliver them.
To those who are to be saved by means of a maiden’s body, he manifests that body to deliver them;
to those who are to be saved by means of a man’s body, he manifests that body to deliver them;
to those who are to be saved by means of a woman’s body, he manifests that body to deliver them.
To those who are to be saved by a youthful body, he manifests that body to transform and deliver them;
to those who are to be saved by a middle-aged body, he manifests that body to transform and deliver them;
to those who are to be saved by an elderly body, he manifests that body to transform and deliver them.
To those who should be saved by means of an inferior body, he manifests that very body to transform and deliver them;
to those who should be saved by means of the body of a butcher or meat-seller, he manifests that very body to transform and deliver them;
to those who should be saved by means of the body of one who is mute or speech-impaired, he manifests that very body to transform and deliver them.
To those who should be delivered by means of a blind or deaf body, he manifests that very body to transform and deliver them;
to those who should be delivered by means of the forms of the three evil realms or the bodies of the human realm, he manifests all of these to transform and deliver them;
to those who should be delivered by means of a celestial body, he manifests that very body to transform and deliver them.

Those who should be delivered through the forms of nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and so forth, he manifests all such forms to bring them to transformation and deliverance;
those who should be delivered through the form of Śakra, he manifests that body to bring them to transformation and deliverance;
those who should be delivered through the form of Brahmā, he manifests that body to bring them to transformation and deliverance.
To those who can be delivered by the body of a World Protector (Lokapāla), he manifests that very body to deliver them;
to those who can be delivered by the body of a Wheel-Turning King (Cakravartin), he manifests that very body to deliver them;
to those who can be delivered by the bodies of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās, he manifests all of these to deliver them.
Those who are to be delivered by means of the body of a śrāvaka, he manifests that very body to deliver them;
those who are to be delivered by means of the body of a pratyekabuddha, he manifests that very body to deliver them;
those who are to be delivered by means of the body of a bodhisattva, he manifests that very body to deliver them.
Those who are to be delivered by means of the body of a Tathāgata, he immediately manifests that body to bring them to transformation and deliverance;
those for whom it is not appropriate to manifest [a physical form] refers to those in the formless realm. From the *Tathāgatācintyaguhyanirdeśamahāyānasūtra*, Fascicle One.
